name: Conch Horn
desc: A big spiral sea conch seen from the side: a stepped cream cone tapering to a sharp spire

problems: The flared lip reads as a separate faceted pink gem or slab stuck onto the front of the shell. It has hard straight-edged corners at (44,-44), (64,-30), (66,0) and (58,30), so it does not look like a smooth flared shell lip that grows out of the body.
The opening (#7a2a22) is a flat angular polygon. It looks like a dark window cut into the lip, not a curved cavity that leads back into the shell.

The spiral barely reads. The spire is a single smooth taper with tiny notches at (-50,-14) and (-36,-22), and the three short tan curves are too weak to show stacked whorls. From the side it looks more like a horn or cornucopia than a conch.
The three spike knobs sit as separate triangles along the top edge. Their bases overlap the body edge only slightly, so at small sizes they look like they are floating.
The body underside is lumpy: the line from (38,22) through (20,30), (0,28) and (-16,20) dips in and out. Where the lip joins the body, around (30,24)–(40,36), there is an awkward notch.

In use: in both held poses the shell is held at chest height with the spire pointing sideways, never at the mouth, so neither one reads as 'blown like a horn'. Scale against the person is good: the shell is about the width of the torso, which reads as big.

for: a big spiral sea conch shell (cream and coral pink, a pointed spire, a flared lip opening) blown like a horn

problems: Style mismatch: the shell is a detailed painting with brush texture, fine ribbing and soft airbrushed gradients. Next to the flat, clean-shaded character it looks pasted in from another art set.
The ragged, spiky frill along the flared lip (about 12 small thorns on the left and right edges) makes the outline busy and noisy at small scale. In the in-hand panels it turns into a pink blob.

The view is upright 3/4, with the spire on top and the lip opening facing the camera. That reads as a decorative seashell, not a horn: there is no mouthpiece end and no clear bell end. The spec also asks for a side view.
At hand scale it is only about torso-width. With little contrast against the teal shirt, the spire and the opening are hard to read in the held panels.
No charcoal or gold accent ties it to the house palette.
